result.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks
result.summary: Neural networks with randomly initialized, fixed weights and trainable biases are universal approximators, yet the dynamics of bias-only training remain largely unexplored. We study these dynamics in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks through activation codes, the binary patterns of active neurons that partition the input space into convex polyhedral regions. We show that the gradients with respect to the biases depend on each input only through its activation code, and hence the training dynamics can be characterized with these codes. In particular, as long as the activation codes remain fixed, training reduces to a linear least-squares problem with the codes as features. Training can then be understood as a sequence of least-squares problems, with transitions occurring when neurons change their activation states. We show that the fraction of switching neurons vanishes as the network widens, and the training dynamics approach those of linear least squares on the initial activation codes in the infinite-width limit. Our experiments support these theoretical findings, showing that while activation switches can noticeably affect training in narrower networks, their relative frequency and the associated changes in the dynamics diminish as the width increases.

AI.brief_summary: 研究单隐层 ReLU 网络在权重随机固定、仅训练偏置时的训练动力学，用「激活码」刻画梯度与输入空间的凸多面体划分，证明激活码不变时训练等价于以激活码为特征的线性最小二乘，并分析宽度增大时神经元切换比例趋于零、动力学收敛到线性最小二乘。
AI.relevance_reason: 激活码作为离散状态把训练分为若干最小二乘阶段、并由切换事件触发状态转移，可能与 latent 推理中内部状态的阶段性切换及宽度/规模对状态稳定性的影响形成概念类比，可供核查其可迁移性。
